interest: This list of papers provides a valuable index of U.S. diplomatic and military surveillance of Japan's educational system during the crucial transitional period of the early 1930s, as the nation shifted toward militarism and intensified nationalism. It highlights how American observers monitored both domestic educational finances—such as central government subsidies for compulsory education during the Great Depression—and ideological trends, including textbook revisions and anti-foreign or anti-Chinese indoctrination. The references to the Young People's School (Seinen Gakkō) and nationalist incidents at Christian institutions like Doshisha University in Kyoto offer vital leads for historians examining prewar youth mobilization and state pressure on private and religious educational establishments.
overview: This file consists of a single Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet for decimal file 894.42 (Internal Affairs of Japan: Education / Correspondence Schools), recording document entries 24 through 30 dating from April 1930 to March 1933 and subsequent years. The listed documents include diplomatic despatches from Tokyo (from Ambassadors William R. Castle, Jr. and W. Cameron Forbes, and Chargé d'Affaires Edwin L. Neville), a despatch from Minister Nelson T. Johnson in China, a report from the Military Attaché in Japan, and a report from the American Consulate in Osaka. The indexed records address Japanese government subsidies for compulsory education in the draft budget submitted to the Diet, the 53rd and 54th annual reports of the Japanese Minister of State for Education, planned textbook revisions reflecting shifting international outlooks, allegations of anti-Chinese and anti-foreign teachings in Japanese schoolbooks, the organization of Young People's Schools (Seinen Gakkō), and nationalist conflicts at Christian institutions, specifically Doshisha University in Kyoto.

subfiles.summary: This sub-file comprises a Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet recording entries 24 through 30 under decimal file 894.42 (Education in Japan). The entries index communications from U.S. diplomatic posts in Japan and China, the Military Attaché, and the Consulate in Osaka between 1930 and 1933 or later. Topics recorded include state budget subsidies for compulsory education to relieve local governments, annual reports of the Japanese Minister of State for Education, planned textbook revisions, anti-foreign and anti-Chinese teachings in schoolbooks, youth education at the Young People's School, and nationalist incidents at Christian institutions including Doshisha University at Kyoto.
